data.title: Anatoly Yakovenko Says Robinhood Revenue Share Covers Solana Trading Fees Four Times Over
data.description: Solana co-founder Anatoly Yakovenko said Robinhood’s revenue share paid to Arbitrum is enough to cover roughly four times its trading fees on Solana. According to ChainCatcher, he said this would allow Robinhood to offer users a fully gas-free trading experience on Solana.

data.title: Solana Co-Founder Says Robinhood Chain Revenue Share Could Cover Four Times Solana's Transaction Fees
data.description:
Solana co-founder Anatoly Yakovenko, known as Toly, said on X that Robinhood Chain's 10% revenue share paid to Arbitrum is enough to cover about four times Solana's transaction fees over the same period. According to Odaily, he added that if the revenue were used to subsidize user transactions, Robinhood Chain could offer a fully gas-free experience.

SolanaNews, citing Blockworks data, previously reported that Robinhood Chain's average transaction fee has recently risen to about $0.40 per transaction, more than 100 times Solana's fee and more than twice Ethereum's.

data.title: SLINK Surges to $80 Million Before Falling More Than 97%
data.description: SLINK briefly surged to a market value of about $80 million after Elon Musk replied to a post from Shivon Zilis' compromised account, according to Onchain Lens monitoring. According to ChainCatcher, multiple traders rushed into the token after the reply, and four traders alone lost about $807,000. SLINK later fell to about $2 million, dropping more than 97% from its peak.

data.title: Bitcoin Film Enters Post-Production With $70 Million Budget
data.description:
The Bitcoin-themed film Bitcoin has entered post-production with an estimated budget of about $70 million. According to ChainCatcher, the movie is directed by Doug Liman and stars Gal Gadot, Casey Affleck, Pete Davidson, and Isla Fisher.

Casey Affleck will play Craig Wright, who has claimed to be Bitcoin's creator, while Pete Davidson will portray his supporter Calvin Ayre. The film has not yet secured a major U.S. distributor or a release date.

Some scenes and lighting were reportedly generated using AI. Some commentators have suggested the film may portray Craig Wright as Satoshi Nakamoto, but the producers have not confirmed that.

data.title: Strategy Says Bitcoin Must Fall 83% for STRC to Reach 1x BTC Rating
data.description:
Strategy said its internal model shows Bitcoin would need to fall 83% from current levels to $13,136 for STRC to reach a 1x BTC Rating. According to Odaily, the metric means the value of Bitcoin reserves equals the nominal debt and preferred stock claims included in the security, and it is not an external credit rating.

The model puts Bitcoin price thresholds at $1,519 for STRF, $13,136 for STRC, $14,198 for STRE, $15,857 for STRK and $17,517 for STRD, while debt has a threshold of zero under the model. Strategy said the BTC Rating does not mean STRC will default, stop paying dividends or trade at a specific price.

As of August 30, Strategy held 845,050 Bitcoin and $6.71 billion in assets. On August 31, the company disclosed a $152 million repurchase of STRC and a $30 million allocation to cash, bringing that balance to $1.61 billion. Its latest Bitcoin purchase added 4,603 Bitcoin for about $369.7 million at an average price of $80,318.

data.title: Circle Details cirBTC Reserve Mechanism and 1:1 BTC Backing
data.description:
Circle said each cirBTC is backed 1:1 by native BTC and can be redeemed for native BTC at the same ratio. According to Odaily, the related BTC is held by a Circle affiliate and custodied by Circle National Trust, which is regulated by the U.S. Office of the Comptroller of the Currency. The reserve assets are separated from Circle’s corporate assets and are used only to protect cirBTC holders’ interests.

cirBTC is currently live on Ethereum. Circle said native support will be added after the Arc mainnet launches, with expansion to more blockchains planned later. Circle also said it provides on-chain reserve verification through a public BTC reserve address and Chainlink Proof of Reserve, allowing market participants to compare reserve holdings with cirBTC circulating supply on supported chains.

data.title: South Korean Court Sentences Man to One Year for Illegal Virtual Asset Cash-Out Service
data.description:
A Chuncheon District Court judge sentenced a 34-year-old man to one year in prison for violating the Act on Reporting and Using Specified Financial Transaction Information. According to Foresight News, the man operated a virtual asset cash-out channel on Telegram from January to June this year, recruited clients, and carried out 152 transactions.

He received a total of about 2.287 million USDT from customers and delivered equivalent cash in person after deducting a 2% to 5% fee. The court said the activity amounted to illegal virtual asset business operations that were not reported to South Korean financial authorities.

data.title: U.S. Used Nvidia Chip Access to Help Secure Armenia-Azerbaijan Peace Deal, Sources Say
data.description:
People involved in the talks said U.S. negotiators used promises of access to Nvidia AI chips to help secure a preliminary peace agreement between Armenia and Azerbaijan last year. According to Odaily, the U.S. also expanded chip purchase approval authority for Armenia’s data center project to encourage its participation in the negotiations.

The arrangement was described as one of the clearest examples so far of what U.S. officials have called "chip diplomacy." The article said the Armenia deal was the Trump administration’s first public use of such a tactic to help reach a peace agreement, after previously using AI hardware in talks with the United Arab Emirates and Saudi Arabia. It also said the agreement further deepened ties between the White House and the world’s largest chipmaker.

data.title: ASIA NIGHT SESSION | Nikkei Futures Rise 810 Points on Waller Dovish Signal; Hang Seng Futures Firm, Korea and Taiwan Shut
data.description:
According to Yonhap, HKET and JPX official data, Asian index-futures traded higher overnight after Federal Reserve Governor Christopher Waller said he would back holding rates at this month's FOMC if incoming data confirm easing inflation pressure. His remarks trimmed rate-hike bets and lifted Wall Street, with the Dow up 1.18%, the S&P 500 up 1.06% and the Nasdaq up 1.40%; the CME-implied odds of a September hold rose to 49.5% from 36.8%, and the 10-year Treasury yield eased 3 basis points to 4.761%. The yen firmed past 156 per dollar.

In Japan's overnight futures on the Osaka Exchange, the near-month Nikkei 225 index futures (September 2026 contract) settled the night session at 65,830, up 810 points, trading between a low of 64,660 and a high of 65,970 from an open of 65,100 (as of 06:00 Japan time, Sept. 5).

Hong Kong's Hang Seng Index night futures closed 10 points higher at 25,667, while the FTSE China A50-linked mainland-shares gauge cited by HKET rose 0.9% to 6,055. Among U.S.-listed proxies, Baidu's American shares traded about 1.7% above their Hong Kong close; converted to Hong Kong dollars, Tencent's ADR was 443.76 (+0.22%), HSBC's ADR 167.96 (+0.75%), Alibaba's U.S. shares 110.98 (+0.80%) and Meituan's ADR 81.50 (-0.31%). In the prior cash session the Hang Seng had closed up 437 points at 25,650.

Taiwan's index-futures night session did not trade, as the Taiwan Futures Exchange runs no after-hours session ahead of the weekend; the market is closed for the night session.

South Korea is omitted this session: no morning report on the KOSPI 200 night-futures close for the overnight period was available, so no night-session figure is reported for Seoul.

data.title: AI TRENDS | Apple’s Foldable iPhone Rumored to Get the Name iPhone Duo
data.description:
The rumored foldable iPhone is now being called iPhone Duo, after earlier names such as iPhone Ultra and iPhone Fold. According to Sina Finance, there is still no evidence that Apple will use the iPhone Duo name, although the possibility remains.

Apple has previously used the Duo brand for the PowerBook Duo notebook line in the 1990s and for the MagSafe Duo charger in the early 2020s. The article says Duo refers to the foldable iPhone’s dual-screen design. Microsoft launched the Surface Duo dual-screen Android phone in 2020, and Intel previously released the popular Core Duo and Core 2 Duo processors.

The report also notes that other rivals use Ultra and Fold naming, including Samsung’s Galaxy S26 Ultra and Galaxy Z Fold8. In April, former Macworld reporter Felipe Esposito cited sources familiar with Apple’s plans as saying the foldable iPhone would be named iPhone Ultra. Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman said many Apple employees call the device iPhone Ultra, but he has never reported with certainty that it will be the product’s official name.

Apple has already used the Ultra name for Apple Watch Ultra, CarPlay Ultra, and the M1 Ultra, M2 Ultra, M3 Ultra, and M5 Ultra chips.

data.title: S&P Dow Jones Indices Announces Changes to S&P 100, S&P 500, and S&P MidCap 400 Constituents
data.description:
S&P Dow Jones Indices announced changes to several index constituents, including the S&P 100, S&P 500, and S&P MidCap 400, with the adjustments set to take effect on September 21, 2026. According to Odaily, the S&P 100 will add Palo Alto Networks, Arista Networks, SanDisk Networks, and Dell Technologies, while Nike, Colgate-Palmolive, and Honeywell Aerospace will be removed.

The S&P 500 will add Bloom Energy, Illumina, and Everpure. The S&P MidCap 400 will add HubSpot, AGNC, Corcept, and Brinker.

data.title: U.S. Military Launches Leak Probe After Sensitive Weapons Stockpile Details Were Exposed
data.description: According to Wallstreetcn, the U.S. military launched a large-scale leak investigation after highly sensitive classified information about U.S. advanced weapons stockpiles was disclosed by the media, and dozens of people, including some top military officials, underwent polygraph tests this summer, including some officials from U.S. Central Command and other combatant command commanders.

data.title: U.S. Federal Judge Rejects Stars and Stripes Publishers' Bid to Block Dismissals
data.description: According to Wallstreetcn, U.S. federal district judge Trevor McFadden on September 4 rejected a temporary restraining order request filed by Stars and Stripes publisher Max Lederer, editor-in-chief Eric Slevin, and Middle East reporter Lara Korte, allowing the U.S. Department of Defense to continue moving forward with their dismissals. The judge said the three had not yet shown that their First Amendment rights were likely to be violated.
